record_type_quote: This study contributes towards the establishment of external validity for Szymanski and Hise's (2000) e-satisfaction model by extending the measurement and predictors of e-satisfaction to a cross-cultural context using a sample of Moroccan online consumers.

targets.evidence_quote: This study contributes towards the establishment of external validity for Szymanski and Hise's (2000) e-satisfaction model by extending the measurement and predictors of e-satisfaction to a cross-cultural context using a sample of Moroccan online consumers.
targets.outcome_quote: In contrast to the original study, product information, rather than convenience was found to be the most important driver of e-satisfaction. In addition, the total effect of convenience on e-satisfaction was found to be significantly less than in the original study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The supplied abstract explicitly contrasts the ranking of the main drivers with the original and reports a significantly smaller convenience effect. All comparisons available in this evidence disagree; the unseen full paper could contain additional comparisons.
